Eight helicopter voices.
Six distinct aircraft.

Compare the new rotor banks and promising effects from Universal Sound FX. Nothing plays automatically; starting a clip pauses the previous one.

Helicopter comparisonUniversal shortlistNew library inventoryOriginal 5 October audit
What is verified: all 40 helicopter source loops were measured; all six game profiles passed mixer, speed selection, loop-wrap, stopped/budget-suppressed silence and cockpit-routing checks.
What remains subjective: identity and final mix balance. These selections were not judged by ear. The spool previews are synthesized demonstrations without distance attenuation, cockpit filtering or surrounding game sounds. Spectral figures describe the fastest source and do not identify real rotor RPM or a helicopter model.

Listen across all eight profiles

The pack contains 168 WAVs: five 16-second loops plus sixteen transition/acceleration/deceleration recordings per family. The game blends adjacent speed loops with actual rotor speed, including coast-down; at most two layers play. The source label “0x” means the lowest audible loop, so stopped rotors are explicitly silent. No independent electric-motor layer has been inferred from these combined recordings.

Previous shared rotor recording for comparison

Legacy Helicopter3 medium exterior loop, 2.91 s. This earlier audit preview has its own review gain and is not loudness-matched to the new spool demonstrations.

Seventeen promising effects to audition next

These are review candidates, not additional game imports. Existing carrier ambience, tracks, doors and servos already have recent integrations; compare these alternatives before replacing them. Locking events, failure detail and sustained crash contact remain useful areas to assess. Loopability and material character still require listening; a filename and a small endpoint discontinuity do not prove a seamless or suitable loop.
